To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) bioabsorbable implants, after hot bending and submergence in buffer at 370 C, tend to lose some, or all (depending on implant thickness and type), of their three-dimensional configuration; (2) this tendency is more pronounced as the duration of the submersion increases; (3) it is more pronounced as additional hot bends are performed on the same implant; (4) it is more severe for thinner implants; (5) it is more significant for implants

(1) bioabsorbable implants lose some, or all (depending on the polymer and thickness), of the angle height when unconstrained in a 37 C water bath; (2) this loss is greater as the number of bending cycles increases; (3) the rate of loss is more pronounced for thinner plates; and (4) the rate of angle loss is dependent on the amount of static weight applied.

(1) the geometric stability of shape adapted bioabsorbable implants is affected by the static loading conditions, (2) this effect is more pronounced with increasing number of cycles of loading, and (3) thicker plates exhibit better stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioabsorbale devices for the treatment of bone and cartilage defects.
the development of bioabsorbale implants that can be shaped to fit the anatomy, intraoperatively.
the development of a bioabsorbable, three-dimensionally adaptable plate for use in craniofacially reconstructive procedures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bioabsorbable implants that are three-dimensionally adapted via heat, and then placed in water at 36-38-C for a period of hours to days, will exhibit some degree of shape loss, which will vary with the polymer formulation, plate thickness, and static load.
the geometric stability of bioabs orbable plates is a function of the polymer composition, plate thickness, and static loading.
shape adaptation of bioabsorble plates, via heating, is not a permanent process.
